summary: How should future Mars astronauts choose a route while investigating waterways in Jezero Crater? A decision engine balancing water-related targets, radiation, terrain and safety.
details:
What is NOVA PROJECT?

NOVA PROJECT is an Unreal Engine 5 simulation designed to help astronauts choose safe and scientifically valuable routes on Mars. The project focuses on Jezero Crater, where stream channels, river pathways, delta formations and flood deposits preserve important information about the movement of water across the Martian surface.

Instead of choosing the shortest route, NOVA PROJECT compares several possible paths and identifies the route that offers the best balance between science, safety and mission resources.

How does it work?

The system combines terrain, geological and radiation information from NASA, ESA and peer-reviewed scientific studies. It evaluates slope, surface roughness, distance, estimated EVA time, radiation exposure, emergency-return distance and the scientific value of geological targets.

The route planner prioritizes features such as stream channels, delta topsets and foresets, Walhalla Glades mudstone, Mount Spoonhead conglomerate and possible carbonate-bearing units. Candidate routes are scored according to their operational cost and expected science return. The selected route is the one that reaches the most valuable targets while keeping risk, energy use and radiation exposure within acceptable limits.

Benefits and intended impact

NOVA PROJECT can help future Mars crews spend less time on inefficient traverses and more time studying high-value geological targets. It also supports radiation-aware planning by considering natural terrain barriers, such as valley walls, that may reduce exposure from parts of the sky.

The project can support geological mapping, sample selection, water-related terrain studies and future in-situ resource utilization planning. Its decision-making approach can also be adapted to the Moon, asteroids and other planetary surfaces.

Tools and data

The prototype was developed with Unreal Engine 5. It uses NASA/JPL Perseverance images, NASA Mars Science Laboratory Radiation Assessment Detector data, Perseverance field mapping, ESA topographic information and peer-reviewed studies of Jezero Crater, its delta, stream channels, flood deposits and geological units.

The final project presentation does not use AI-generated imagery. The visuals come from NASA, ESA and the cited scientific publications.

Creativity and team considerations

The creative aspect of NOVA PROJECT is its combination of science planning and astronaut safety in one route-selection system. The team considered scientific value, slope, roughness, radiation, energy, time, emergency access, sample potential and data reliability.

The system is also flexible. Mission planners can change the importance of science, safety, radiation or travel time depending on the mission goal. This makes NOVA PROJECT an adaptable decision-support tool rather than a route that works for only one scenario.

Development status and limitations

Because of the limited development time and resources available during the challenge, we could not complete every planned part of the project. Unlike many projects that use AI extensively to speed up development, NOVA PROJECT was developed with very limited AI assistance. This allowed us to maintain greater control over the scientific content and the 3D design, but it also made development slower and contributed to the project not being completed within the submission period. Our main differentiator is that NOVA PROJECT is designed as a 3D Mars simulation in Unreal Engine 5, rather than a 2D map or a website-based concept. The prototype demonstrates the core idea and decision logic, while future work will include a more complete 3D environment, interactive route selection, terrain-based navigation and a more detailed astronaut simulation.
